related_policies: Itemized Bill, Itemized Bill Review for Inpatient Routine Services

extracted_content.content: Related policies: Itemized Bill, Itemized Bill Review for Inpatient Routine Services

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: Facility billing guidelines for the UB-04 claim form, also known as the CMS-1450, and the 837 institutional electronic equivalent require providers to bill revenue codes to describe services furnished. Revenue codes are categorical and do not provide detailed descriptions of specific items, supplies and services provided during an outpatient encounter. Humana may request an itemized bill for an outpatient facility claim to verify that billed revenue codes represent charges for appropriately billed items, supplies and services. Routine items, supplies and services already included in other outpatient charges are not separately billable.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. This policy applies to outpatient facilities that include, but are not limited to, hospital outpatient departments and ambulatory surgery centers. To separately bill for items, supplies and services, a provider must consistently follow its customary charging practices for all Medicare and non-Medicare patients, for all payers and health plans. Humana sometimes reviews an itemized bill for an outpatient encounter to determine whether supplies, items and services specified on the itemized bill are separately billable. The following supplies, items and services are typically not separately billable and, therefore, not separately payable from primary service charge(s). Please note that the examples given do not represent an exhaustive list.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: Any supplies, items and services that, under customary charging practices, are included in charges for a specific service or in charges for the delivery of services in a specific location. Examples of included supplies and services are bandages, IV flushing, dressing changes, equipment monitoring and routine nursing care and assessments.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: All items and supplies that may be purchased over the counter, such as personal care items, ice packs, alcohol wipes and cotton balls.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: All reusable items, supplies and equipment that are provided to all patients on a routine basis during an outpatient encounter; this applies to all outpatient encounters. Examples of reusable items, supplies and equipment are cardiac monitors and durable medical equipment (DME) items used while in an outpatient facility.

reimbursement_guidelines.title: Reimbursement Guidelines
reimbursement_guidelines.content:
In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. This policy applies to outpatient facilities that include, but are not limited to, hospital outpatient departments and ambulatory surgery centers. To separately bill for items, supplies and services, a provider must consistently follow its customary charging practices for all Medicare and non-Medicare patients, for all payers and health plans. Humana sometimes reviews an itemized bill for an outpatient encounter to determine whether supplies, items and services specified on the itemized bill are separately billable. The following supplies, items and services are typically not separately billable and, therefore, not separately payable from primary service charge(s). Please note that the examples given do not represent an exhaustive list.

Any supplies, items and services that, under customary charging practices, are included in charges for a specific service or in charges for the delivery of services in a specific location. Examples of included supplies and services are bandages, IV flushing, dressing changes, equipment monitoring and routine nursing care and assessments.

All items and supplies that may be purchased over the counter, such as personal care items, ice packs, alcohol wipes and cotton balls.

All reusable items, supplies and equipment that are provided to all patients on a routine basis during an outpatient encounter; this applies to all outpatient encounters. Examples of reusable items, supplies and equipment are cardiac monitors and durable medical equipment (DME) items used while in an outpatient facility.

In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana Medicaid plans review outpatient itemized bills with routine services according to applicable state Medicaid agency requirements.
